question: The Strategic Compass for Security and Defence pays particular attention to enhancing the Union’s role in intelligence coordination. It sets out the concrete ambition to further expand the joint intelligence analysis capacity by 2025 and to strengthen the EU Satellite Centre. However, questions arise in this regard, inter alia because of the vagueness with which these objectives are set out in the Compass. 1.
What specific objectives are to be achieved by 2025 and what means are to be provided by then?

The Compass implies that new resources will be made available. Can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy be more specific: what do the new resources amount to and where will they come from?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.3.2024) The need to strengthen the EU Satellite Centre (SatCen)1 derives from the operational situation and the need for SatCen to continuously deliver when confronted to a growing demand for SatCen products and services linked to the degrading security situation worldwide.

In the context of the objectives and ambitions set out in the Strategic Compass2 in August 2023, the High Representative/Vice-President called for a meeting of the SatCen board in Madrid, to discuss SatCen’s future objectives. The Ministers gave political guidance on SatCen’s future development and on possible ways to boost the EU’s autonomous geospatial intelligence analysis capability.

This will translate in a development plan for SatCen, which will be submitted to the board in the course of 2024. The development plan could imply additional voluntary contributions from Member States to the SatCen budget. For instance some countries already provided voluntary contributions to SatCen budget in 2022. Funding options will be discussed with Member States.
